verdict.rationale: The evidence makes clear that Column is itself the charter holder, not middleware: its llms.txt identifies Column N.A. as a nationally chartered bank, a Column engineer describes it as an issuing bank, it runs its own direct Federal Reserve ACH integration, and accounts are opened as FDIC-insured accounts at Column. The 'what happens to my customers if the platform fails' half is only implied by the FDIC-insured label, with no documentation of failure handling or of how FBO pass-through coverage works. Missing for 10: documentation of failure/resolution scenarios for end customers, explicit pass-through FDIC insurance treatment for FBO/sweep accounts, independent corroboration of the charter and insurance structure.
